The form makes an unretired advance the personal liability of the recipient. Blocking further advances is the mildest enforcement of that; confirm against existing practice.

Same rule and figure as EXPENSE's own PAYMENT_METHOD_THRESHOLD_NGN (DEL-AC-FRM-002 Rev 05 footer), applied to TotalAmountNgn via CashAdvanceRequest.ApplyPaymentMethodPolicy since an advance has no net-payable concept of its own. A future rate change is a new row here with a later effectiveFrom, not an edit to this one -- see WorkflowDefinitionExtensions.GetPolicyValue.

transitions.guard: LineCount > 0 && TotalAmountNgn > 0 && HasValidAllocation == true && HasOverdueAdvance == false
transitions.guardMessage: Add at least one line, select a project or cost centre code, and retire any overdue advance before requesting another.
transitions.note: Straight to the Head of Department. Version 3 routed through a line manager first; Desicon has one approval on the requesting side.

transitions.guardMessage: You cannot verify your own request.
Capture the Treasury number before passing this to the Finance Manager.
transitions.note: Cost Control checks that the advance is costed to the right centre. A separate desk from the Treasury officer who posts it at AWAITING_POSTING and releases the cash at CASH_RELEASE -- version 2 modelled them as one role, which let the same person check the costing, post against their own check, and hand over the money.

transitions.guardMessage: You cannot approve your own advance request.
transitions.note: The Accounts Manager releases the advance for treatment. She does not release the money -- that is the Director of Finance's alone.

transitions.guardMessage: You cannot approve payment of your own advance.
transitions.note: The gate. No cash leaves Desicon without the Director of Finance, and version 1 of this definition had no such step -- the Accounts Officer could release cash on the Accounts Manager's approval alone. Unconditional here, unlike expense: an advance always pays somebody.

transitions.guardMessage: Enter the Business Central document number for this posting.
transitions.note: The Accounts Officer posts in Business Central, then records here that she has and under which document number. No journal lines are captured: BC owns the ledger, and a second copy in another system is two versions of the truth waiting to disagree. The document number is the only key joining this approval trail to the ledger entry, which is why it is required.

Cash release starts the retirement clock. Working hours against the NG_STANDARD calendar. PaymentMethod is derived by CashAdvanceRequest.ApplyPaymentMethodPolicy at submission/recalculation time, not captured here -- Finance cannot choose it at release.
Recipient's Acknowledgement. Recorded for the audit trail and the printed form; the clock already started at release.

transitions.guardMessage: This advance already carries no balance.
A balance remains outstanding on this advance.

transitions.note: Terminal disposal for an advance that will not be retired. Requires a reason and is reported to management.

transitions.guardMessage: A balance remains outstanding on this advance.
This advance already carries no balance.

retirementClock.note: Per Finance direction 31 Jul 2026. On a 9-hour working day this makes 24h = 2.67 working days and 72h = 8 working days. Change 'unit' to CalendarHours if that proves not to be the intent.

note: Version 3 splits FinanceOfficer into CostControlOfficer and TreasuryOfficer. Version 2 recorded that Cost Control and the Accounts Officer who posts in Business Central were the same people; they are not. They are separate desks with separate mailboxes (costcontrol@ and treasury@), and one role covering both meant a single person could verify the costing, post it, and release the cash -- with the posting notification going to the wrong desk, so the person who had to act was never told. Version 2 remains published for requests already open under it; see cash-advance.v2.workflow.json and docs/15-Go-Live-Checklist.md section 3.
amendment: 19 Aug 2026: version 4 removes the LINE_MANAGER step. Desicon has ONE approval before Cost Control -- the Head of Department. Version 3 modelled two, which for Desicon would have meant the same person approving the same request twice. No version 3 file is retained because the database was reset for UAT and nothing was ever pinned to it. See docs/15 section 3.
